description: A source-preserving catalogue of reports and commentary from Tafsīr al-Thawrī, Ibn Wahb, Mujāhid, Yaḥyā ibn Sallām, and Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, organized by Qurʾanic surah and verse where source citations permit.

organization.method: Reports are placed under every explicit Qurʾanic verse citation; reports without a verse locator but with an explicit surah name are placed at that surah level. The source volume and page, transmission, Arabic text, English translation, notes, and printed numbering are retained. Unlocated source reports remain fully listed by source volume. For Tafsīr Mujāhid, Arabic source section headings also place untagged records at surah level, with no verse inferred; Arabic-only text is preserved verbatim. For Yaḥyā ibn Sallām, page-sized Arabic source records were split at bracketed Qurʾanic citations; cited verses in the current surah determine verse placement, while cross-surah citations remain marked as cross-references. Uncited material stays at the source surah level. Muqātil ibn Sulaymān: the four-volume Tafsīr has 114 formal surah headings; numbered verse-ending markers are applied within each active surah, with unmarked page fragments retained at surah level. Opening material, end matter, and the editor’s fifth-volume study are kept separately and not misattributed as Muqātil’s verse exegesis.

placementAdjustments.reason: The source export carries passages from al-Muʾminūn under its preceding al-Ḥajj section heading; the quoted verse wording identifies the correct sura.
These verse numbers exceed al-Furqān's 77 verses; the quoted passages belong to the following sura, ash-Shuʿarāʾ.
The catalog marks verse 910 as a sic and identifies the intended verse as 10.
The cited 7–11 range is explicitly from al-Wāqiʿah, not Fāṭir; without a local verse locator the passage stays at surah level.
